solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Speaking out, you spill the beans on drugs

indicators.note: speaking out tells us to judge the words by how they are said rather than how they are written

blocks.note: to sing is slang for confessing or spilling the beans, so the phrase is 'you sing'

explanation.surface: An informant is being told they are high when they talk to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'you sing' runs together into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is using is currently taking illegal substances, an everyday slang sense of the verb.

clue.text: Ignorant, as police may be about how investigation ends

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept
about means surrounding, so the longer piece wraps around the shorter one

blocks.note: police officers on the beat wear uniform
the last letter of investigation

explanation.surface: Officers are kept in the dark about how an inquiry turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How investigation ends' points to its final letter, not to the outcome of a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ignorant means lacking knowledge, which is exactly what not having been told anything implies.

clue.text: Upright character recalled writing practice

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the following piece runs backwards up the column

blocks.note: the capital letter I is a single upright stroke
MS, short for manuscript, is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a handwriting drill involving tall vertical letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is a distinctive doctrine or practice, the noun formed from suffixes like those in socialism.

clue.text: “Great” millionaire happy to save high-street bank

indicators.note: to save something is to hold onto it, so one piece keeps another inside it

blocks.note: an older sense of gay is cheerful or merry
TSB is a British retail bank found on high streets

explanation.surface: A wealthy man is glad to rescue a failing local bank.
explanation.walkthrough: A high street is the main shopping street of a British town, where retail banks have branches.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay Gatsby is the rich title character of Fitzgerald's novel The Great Gatsby, hence the quotation marks.

clue.text: One keeps stocking up pubs, periodically interrupting consumer

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept
something that interrupts breaks into the middle of another thing

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
a consumer is someone who spends money

explanation.surface: A landlord restocks pubs while a customer keeps barging in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocking up' looks like shop restocking but means holding a stocking up.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is a clasp-ended strap that holds a woman's stocking up on the leg.

clue.text: Bottom pinched by admirer, one checking for dodgy characters?

indicators.note: something pinched is held tightly between, so one piece sits gripped inside another

blocks.note: a suitor is a man who admires and courts a woman
the bottom of a river or sea is its bed

explanation.surface: A lewd admirer pinches someone's behind, and a security officer checks for suspicious people.
explanation.walkthrough: The dodgy characters are faulty letters on a page, not shady people.
explanation.definitionFit: A subeditor corrects copy before publication, hunting for typographical errors and wrong letters.

clue.text: Why don’t we put up a stone monument?

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means written from bottom to top

blocks.note: 'let's' is the suggestion 'why don't we?'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone proposes erecting a memorial stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stela is an upright carved stone slab used in antiquity as a monument or gravestone.

clue.text: Participants in equestrian competitions never set off

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Riders entered in horse trials who never start their rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventers compete in eventing, the horse-riding discipline combining dressage, cross-country and show jumping.

clue.text: Criminal relented, if receiving answer showing respect

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so an extra letter joins the group
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker softens and becomes polite once given a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Deferential behaviour yields politely to another's authority, displaying courteous regard.

clue.text: Possibly magical symbol that has left Potter unexcited?

indicators.note: has means contains, so the letters are already present within the following words

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A spell symbol fails to thrill the boy wizard Harry Potter.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes are letters of old Germanic alphabets, often credited with mystical or occult power, hence possibly magical.

clue.text: Fixed this person’s shoe worn by Bill in America

indicators.note: a shoe that is worn has a foot inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: this person is the speaker, so this person's is I'M
a mule is a backless slipper or shoe
Americans call a restaurant or bar bill a tab

explanation.surface: Someone's shoe has been repaired and worn by an American called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name but is the American word for a bill to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immutable cannot change, so it stays permanently set like a fixed rule.

clue.text: Like Sprite? A German drinks litres loudly

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so one piece swallows the others

blocks.note: ein is German for a
L is the abbreviation for litres
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A German downs litres of the fizzy lemonade Sprite, noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: L and F go inside EIN, after the E. The capital S disguises a fairy as the soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is a fairy or elf, so being elfin means having that small delicate fairylike quality.

clue.text: Think e.g. ham sandwiches fine? This makes me despair

indicators.note: a sandwich holds a filling between its slices, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: to feel something can be to believe or think it
a ham is an overacting performer
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether ham sandwiches are acceptable and finds the thought depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ham looks like meat for a sandwich but is a poor performer, and sandwiches is the instruction to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: The feel-bad factor is a general mood of public gloom, something that causes widespread despondency.

clue.text: Making smooth arts broadcast, Sky’s brilliant feature

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into another order

blocks.note: evening out a surface makes it smooth
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A TV channel smooths out its arts output, and Sky has a brilliant programme on.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky reads like the British broadcaster; it is the actual sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening star is Venus seen after sunset, the brightest object in the night sky apart from the Moon.

clue.text: Agree to keep frames of Monet and Rothko around in collection

indicators.note: a frame is the outer edge of a picture, so only the outside letters are kept
turned around means facing the other way, so the kept letters run backwards
to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: to assent is to agree
the first and last letters
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A gallery agrees to hang framed Monet and Rothko works in its collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The two painters' frames are joined first and the pair is turned back as one unit before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An assortment is a varied mixture of things gathered together, a miscellany.

clue.text: Ways for Edith Piaf to show regrets

blocks.note: first meaning: French streets, as the French singer would say
second meaning: is sorry about

explanation.surface: The French singer of Non, je ne regrette rien finds ways to express remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: Piaf is famous for singing that she regrets nothing, which makes the surface ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue is the French noun for street and also the English verb meaning to feel sorrow over something.

clue.text: Love to slip in appreciative remark for soldiers

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
thanks is a remark of appreciation
to err is to make a slip

explanation.surface: Someone is told to drop a word of affection into a thank-you note for the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Slip is what goes in, not the instruction to move love; love simply comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Other ranks are the enlisted soldiers in the British army, everyone who is not a commissioned officer.

clue.text: English chaps are dilettantes, only half-heartedly open to improvement

indicators.note: half-hearted means half the heart is missing, so one of the two central letters goes

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
chaps are men
dilettantes dabble in their interests

explanation.surface: Englishmen are amateurs who are only half committed but could do better.
explanation.walkthrough: DABBLE has a double B at its heart; dropping one B leaves DABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emendable can be corrected or revised, so it is capable of being made better.

clue.text: On same ground, a header from Newcastle United

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and reformed
a header is the top, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
taken as written; also part of the fodder
the first letter

explanation.surface: At the same football ground, a Newcastle United player scores with his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like part of the club name but is the definition. Newcastle United is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting as one man means everyone moving together in complete agreement, which is being united.

clue.text: Fail to see sign introduced by European delegates

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
to miss something is to fail to see it
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: European delegates overlook a signpost they were shown.
explanation.walkthrough: Introduced by puts E at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Emissaries are envoys sent on a mission, representatives acting on someone's behalf.

clue.text: Queen once performed last in Glasto

indicators.note: the last in a word is its final letter, so just that one is taken

blocks.note: performed means did, as in did a task
the final letter

explanation.surface: A former queen of pop played a closing set at Glastonbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasto is the nickname of the Glastonbury music festival; the singer Dido has performed there.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the legendary founder and ruler of Carthage, a queen of ancient times.

clue.text: Boring rhubarb — this can make fruit crumble

blocks.note: a dry speech is a boring one
rhubarb and rot are both slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: A dull rhubarb pudding, with a nod to fruit crumble.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhubarb looks like the dessert filling but means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungal decay that leaves wood, and some fruits and tubers, powdery so that they break apart.

clue.text: After some green tea, pressure group attempted coup

blocks.note: gunpowder is a variety of Chinese green tea rolled into pellets
P is the abbreviation for pressure
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: After tea, a lobby group tries to seize power.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1605 conspiracy to blow up Parliament is remembered in Britain on Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gunpowder Plot was Guy Fawkes's failed scheme to kill King James I, a thwarted overthrow of government.

clue.text: Young flier heading skyward without impediment

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading skyward means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: W/O is the abbreviation for without
a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A young pilot takes off unhindered.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a baby owl, a bird that will fly once it has fledged.

clue.text: Learner sinking in swimming pool one’s adored

indicators.note: in a down entry, sinking means moving towards the bottom, so a letter drops from top to foot

blocks.note: L is the learner-driver plate
a lido is an open-air swimming pool; this is what follows its first letter

explanation.surface: A beginner goes under at the baths.
explanation.walkthrough: The L at the top of LIDO sinks to the bottom, giving IDOL.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a person who is worshipped or greatly admired, an object of adoration.

clue.text: Old lady carries you across the Channel in fact

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a dam is a mother, especially of an animal
tu is French for you; France is across the Channel from Britain

explanation.surface: A mother carries her child over to France.
explanation.walkthrough: Old lady is slang for mother, and dam is the word used for the mother of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information, a given fact used as the basis of reasoning.

clue.text: Hedonist not half like Mr Wooster around noon

indicators.note: not half means only half is used, so the back half of the word is dropped
around means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round another

blocks.note: taken as written
Bertie Wooster is P.G. Wodehouse's comic gentleman
N is short for noon

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker is only partly similar to Wodehouse's idle Bertie round lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside BERTIE before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertine is a dissolute person given to sensual pleasures, someone who pursues gratification freely.

clue.text: Yours truly drained cloudy bitter

indicators.note: drained means emptied of its contents, so only the outside letters remain

blocks.note: yours truly is the speaker, so I
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: I finished a pint of murky bitter beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter looks like the British beer in the surface; it is the adjective for cold weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter weather is piercingly cold, and icy describes a temperature that freezes.

clue.text: Glasses upset — ten Grolsch bottles overturned

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the letters are contained in the words
overturned means turned over, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word to the start of the third, ignoring the dash

explanation.surface: Drinking glasses are knocked over, along with ten bottles of Dutch lager.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasses suggests drinking vessels beside the beer; it means spectacles. Grolsch is a Dutch lager.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles held up to the eyes on a long handle.

clue.text: Seek someone the church approves of for a date

blocks.note: to try for something is to seek it
ST, short for saint, a person the church has canonised

explanation.surface: Looking for a respectable partner to go out with.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a romantic appointment between lovers, a secret meeting arranged in advance.
